input.assumptions: <parameter name="assumptions">["The provided rate card is a PLACEHOLDER: a single 'Team member' role at $75/hour with 1 FTE available. No real team composition (e.g. dedicated backend/frontend/QA/PM roles) or individual rates have been set. All costs below are therefore indicative only and must be re-estimated once actual roles and hourly rates are assigned.", "No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project; estimates are derived purely from story points and task descriptions, not from past velocity or cost data.", "Story points are converted to effort using a rough heuristic of 6 hours per point for typical feature work, adjusted upward for tasks with high integration/compliance/data risk (e.g. payment integration, legacy migration, RBAC) and downward for well-scoped UI-only tasks.", "With only 1 FTE available on the single 'Team member' role, all 24 backlog items must be delivered sequentially by one person. At ~1,800 productive hours/year (37.5 hrs/week after overhead), the full backlog (~1,000+ hours) represents roughly 7-8 months of continuous solo work, meaning the role is staffed far too thinly for this backlog's scope and timeline expectations.", "Because there is only one role, no cross-role breakdown (e.g. separate QA, DevOps, PM) is possible; all hours are attributed to 'Team member'. This likely understates true cost since specialist work (security review, DBA-led migration, UX design) would normally command different rates.", "Priority breakdown totals are calculated by summing the estimated cost of tasks in each priority bucket, using the same $75/hr rate applied to all hours.", "Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for typical SaaS/infra costs (Stripe fees are transactional, not included; staging/CI hosting, monitoring tooling, and legacy Oracle migration tooling/licensing) since no vendor quotes were supplied.", "Scenario totals (P50/P80/P95) reflect uncertainty in a single-person delivery of a 24-item backlog with several high-risk items (payment integration, data migration, RBAC), where estimation error and rework risk are elevated."]

nonLabourLines.description: CI/CD and staging environment hosting (cloud infra, first year)
Stripe integration setup and PCI-related tooling/testing
Legacy Oracle migration tooling / temporary read-replica licensing
Email delivery service (transactional email, e.g. SES/SendGrid) - annual

input.reasoning: Effort was estimated per backlog item using story points as a proxy for complexity, converted at roughly 6 hours/point for standard items, with adjustments: payment integration, legacy migration, RBAC, and 2FA were weighted up for integration/compliance risk; simple UI or config tasks (contract tests, decommissioning) weighted down. Total estimated effort across the 24 items is approximately 1,180 hours. Since the rate card only defines one generic 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE, all hours are booked to that single line, producing a P50 labour cost of $88,500. Non-labour costs cover infrastructure, third-party tooling, and one external audit, adding roughly $14,000. Scenario uncertainty (P80/P95) reflects the compounding risk of a single-person team absorbing urgent/high-risk items (payments, migration, security) with no redundancy or specialist skill separation, and the strong likelihood of underestimation on integration-heavy tasks (PW-7, PW-8, PW-4). Priority breakdown sums the labour cost of tasks grouped by their stated priority at the same flat rate.

reductions.description: Descope Admin back-office for support staff (PW-18, Low priority, 13 points) to a later phase; support agents can use existing admin tooling temporarily.
reductions.effect: Removes an entire feature from this delivery phase, freeing ~78 hours.

reductions.description: Defer Usage analytics and reporting (PW-19, Low, 8 pts) and Contract tests against helpdesk API (PW-23, Low, 5 pts) to a post-launch backlog.
reductions.effect: Removes ~78 hours of low-priority, non-blocking work from the initial cost estimate.

reductions.description: Reduce scope of Multi-currency support (PW-14, 13 pts) to launch with USD-only and add EUR/PLN in a later release.
reductions.effect: Cuts estimated effort on PW-14 roughly in half (~48 hours saved) by removing FX-rate automation and settlement logic for two currencies at launch.

reductions.description: Use a managed migration/ETL SaaS tool instead of custom-built legacy Oracle migration scripts for PW-8, reducing custom engineering hours.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~100 hours of bespoke migration coding/testing by leveraging off-the-shelf ETL tooling, though tool licensing cost (already included in non-labour) offsets some savings.

reductions.description: Defer the external Accessibility audit (non-labour line) and instead do an internal manual review pass using free tooling (axe, Lighthouse) at this stage.
reductions.effect: Removes the $2,500 external audit line item; formal audit can be scheduled closer to a public launch.

reductions.description: Postpone Decommission the legacy portal (PW-24, Low, 8 pts) until the new portal has been live and stable for a full billing cycle.
reductions.effect: Removes ~48 hours from this phase; legacy system continues running in parallel a bit longer at minor ongoing hosting cost not included here.
